title: Let agents run and ship your live product hourly
summary: Spawn's Jacob Sansbury says a swarm of agents develops the game autonomously, shipping to production every hour and spending over $3M a month on AI tokens.
agent_role: Agents read errors, bug reports and metrics, decide whether to fix issues, change live code and ship to production hourly; humans set the overall system and treat gaps in shipping as top incidents.
outcome: Author reports agents ship to production hourly, about 60% of work starts from a production error or bug report, and they spend over $3M a month on tokens (30x payroll).
what_they_did: Jacob Sansbury describes building Spawn, a multiplayer game where players prompt an in-game agent to change the world. A swarm of frontier-model agents develops it autonomously. The agents read every error, bug report and metric, decide what to fix, change the live code and ship to production every hour. The in-game agent files its own bug reports straight to an agent that triages them.
how_it_went: He reports shipping to production hourly, with an hour without a ship treated as the most severe incident. About 60% of work starts from a production error or bug report, and broken changes roll back in 30 seconds.
worth_knowing: The setup costs over $3 million a month in model tokens (30x their payroll) and relies on fast rollback; Simon Willison doubts this style suits all software.
prompt: Set up a loop where my coding agents own our live product. Have them read production errors, user bug reports, logs and metrics, then decide for each one whether it is a real bug, a won't-fix, or a design decision that needs me. For real bugs, draft the fix and show me the change and a rollback plan before shipping. Keep a short log of what shipped and why. Flag anything risky or irreversible and wait for my approval before deploying to production.

curation.rationale: A detailed, striking real-world case of a swarm of agents autonomously developing and shipping a live product hourly, with specific numbers and workflow details.
